column1: # Anchor tasks — the 88 modules from ANCHORS.tsv that face outside and are not
# anchored yet. Generated 2026-08-01. Read ANCHORS.tsv's header first.
# THE JOB: move the expected values in the tests from "we wrote them, from our
# own reading of the spec" to "they came from outside". The foreign tool
# normally runs ONCE, at capture time; the bytes it produced are committed as
# literals and the test stays offline, deterministic and dependency-free.
# SOURCE   VECTOR:<where>  published byte-level vectors covering the gap
#          CLI:<tool>      a command-line tool can emit or check the bytes
#          DAEMON:<tool>   needs a service standing up — much dearer
#          CAPTURE:<where> real artifacts obtainable from a public source
#          NONE            nothing external exists; a legitimate end state
# COST     S  drop in published vectors, or re-run a harness THAT ALREADY
#             EXISTS here with a different input
#          M  build a harness around a CLI, or transcribe a vector set
#          L  stand up a daemon/toolchain, or write a foreign-format parser
#          -  SOURCE is NONE, nothing to do
# ⚠ TWO TRAPS, both already paid for once in this repo:
#   1. Do NOT close one of these by un-skipping a live test into the default
#      gate. Capture the bytes once, commit them, keep the test offline. A
#      flake in the gate costs more than the anchor is worth (see cba13a4).
#   2. NEVER compute a "vector" from our own output. An open, labelled gap is
#      strictly better than a fake anchor.
# ⚠ THIS IS A LOWER BOUND. Classification is per module, so a module that is
#   EXTERNAL overall can still have one uncovered path inside it — enip is
#   EXTERNAL (goldens captured from cpppo/pycomm3) yet its symbolic-segment
#   pad byte is never exercised, because the one captured sample has an
#   even-length tag name. Those per-path gaps are not counted here.
